newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast crudes fall as ANS discount widens.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast crudes fall as ANS discount widens.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crudes fell Friday, after Exxon sold two cargoes of Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude, the region's benchmark, at lower prices, traders said.
Exxon sold about 400,000 barrels of ANS to Shell's Anacortes, Wash., refinery for June delivery at $1.48 a barrel under June West Texas Intermediate/Cushing crude.
Neither side confirmed the deal, which was done late Thursday.
Tosco confirmed Friday they bought 400,000 barrels of ANS at $1.50 early in the day.
The minus $1.50 deal represents a 18-cent-a-barrel fall from May 5, when ANS sold for $1.32 under June WTI.
The wider discounts caused outright ANS prices to end the day down eight cents a barrel from Thurday to $18.85-19.05.
BP, the grade's biggest producer, withdrew its minus $1.15 offer from the market.
High volumes of imports have weakened demand from West Coast refiners, with Chevron rumored to be bring in Arab light and medium crudes for June, traders said.

Chevron and Tosco's heavy reliance on foreigns for June has also cut demand for lighter California San Joaquin Valley (SJV) grades. Those refiners, along with Ultramar, normally buy SJV as a component of Line 63, a ANS lookalike.

Tosco has stopped buying spot barrels of SJV light for its Wilmington refinery, formerly Unocal's, and some traders say the move will help soften SJV prices for their San Francisco plants, which take a larger volume of Valley crudes.
Meanwhile, the U.S. Department of Energy sold 5,075 barrels-per-day (bpd) of Elk Hills light crude to EOTT Energy for June and July delivery.
Traders said Atlantic Richfield Co. was close to buying two 400,000 barrel cargoes of Mesa crude, a Venezuelan lookalike to Alaska North Slope (gravity 30 degrees), for June delivery.
Another major buyer, Texaco, was well supplied for June after taking two to three cargoes of Oriente, traders said.
Kern River crude was unchanged early Friday at $14.01/14.11 a barrel.
Wilmington and Line 63 markets remained idle.
